F01.question: I området Recursive self-improvement, vad är de två senaste nyheterna och vad handlar de om?
F01.answer:
The two most recent papers on Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) in the provided sources are:

[30] ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents, which introduces an interactive scientific research workspace that brings continually improving scientific agents into researchers' workflows. It implements a "recursive-in-recursive self-improvement" paradigm where the inner recursion improves the harness with the model fixed, while the outer recursion trains the model under the improved harness, enabling harness evolution to shape training experience and model learning to create new opportunities for harness adaptation [30].

[31] ModularRSI: Modular and Generalizable Recursive Harness Self-Improvement, which proposes a benchmark-disjoint, contrastive, and modular framework for generalizable harness evolution. It decomposes the evolvable harness into five functional modules (Agent Loop, Tool Use, Observation Management, Context Management, and Task Completion Detection) that evolve independently within restricted modification scopes before being integrated into a unified harness, with 2,000 executable evolution tasks curated from external sources to support benchmark-disjoint evolution [31].

F02.question: Vad har hänt med GUI agents den senaste månaden?
F02.answer:
Based on the provided sources, several significant developments have occurred with GUI agents in the last month (August-September 2026):

Researchers have introduced new benchmarks to diagnose limitations in GUI agents. [26] developed GUI-Primitives, a 994-item benchmark evaluating spatial reasoning failures in vision-language GUI grounding, revealing that models reach at most 32% strict point-in-box accuracy on spatial reasoning tasks.

[27] introduced AnTrap, a comprehensive benchmark that injects dynamic perturbations into agent execution trajectories, revealing that even the strongest GUI models suffer significant performance degradation when encountering runtime anomalies like unexpected pop-ups.

Several new GUI agent frameworks have been presented: [28] introduced LLaDA-UI, a 16.7B-parameter MoE-based, block-wise diffusion vision-language GUI agent that outperforms Qwen2.5-VL-7B and surpasses Qwen3-VL-8B on four of six reported GUI benchmarks.

[29] presented UI-Mate, a foundation GUI agent that integrates an environment-grounded training stack with in-context demonstration learning, setting a new open-weight state of the art on general computer-use benchmarks with 77.0% on OSWorld-Verified and 66.2% on WindowsAgentArena.

[30] introduced UI-Venus-2, a general-purpose foundation GUI agent designed to operate across mobile, web, and desktop environments through a unified closed-loop reasoning-action framework, expanding coverage to more than 170 multilingual mobile apps and native desktop operating systems.

[25] developed MobilePA-Bench, an interactive, stateful, and tool-centric benchmark for evaluating mobile planner agents across 13 functional domains and 212 realistic mobile tools, highlighting challenges in mobile agent planning and tool usage.

F03.question: Vad är det absolut  senaste inom Video genereation och är det hårdvaru- eller mjukvarurelaterat?
F03.answer: The absolute latest in video generation is PhysStream [31], which introduces an autoregressive model for physics-grounded image-to-video synthesis. It incorporates structured scene memory (positional maps and object tracking maps derived online from previously generated frames) and supports fine-grained motion control via sparse velocity-increment signals that encode physical quantities. This is a software-based approach, as it describes a model architecture and training methodology for interactive, mid-generation control over multi-object tabletop rigid-body scenes, reducing motion distribution distance by 33% and trajectory error by 12% over baselines.

F07.question: Vad säger forskningen om text-to-video den senaste månaden?
F07.answer:
The research on text-to-video in the last month includes several key developments. JoyAI-Echo-1.5, a unified audio-visual generation system, introduces composable cross-shot memory and speaker cues from speech-filtered audio to enable persistent character appearance and voice identity across text, image, and memory conditioning, while maintaining visual quality and audio-visual synchronization [2]. 

Temporal Context Routing (TCR) has been developed to address timing issues in script-driven content creation, mapping script timing onto the shared temporal axis of video and audio generation. This reduces Shot Boundary MAE by 96% (from 1.11s to 0.042s) and raises Dialogue Acc@0.5s from 28.3% to 84.1% [22].

FIRM-Video introduces a checklist-driven framework for text-to-video reward modeling that decomposes prompts into weighted atomic requirements for instruction following, constructs prompt-calibrated checks for world coherence, and applies visual defect taxonomies for perceptual quality. The Qwen3-VL-based FIRM-Video-8B achieves the best overall MAE on FIRM-Video-Bench [29].

DF26, a novel benchmark for detecting AI-generated videos containing fully synthetic clips from text-to-video models, reveals that both human performance and state-of-the-art deepfake detectors are close to random chance in identifying AI-generated content, highlighting limitations in current evaluation protocols [31].

A survey of inference-efficiency mechanisms in video and audiovisual LLMs, including text-to-video models, analyzes bottlenecks across frame sampling, modality encoding, connector-level token reduction, and LLM prefilling and decoding, aiming to reduce computational costs for real-time deployment [30].

F08.question: Nämns LEGO i någon artikel och i så fall, sammanfatta vad de handlar om.
F08.answer: Yes, LEGO is mentioned in source [32] as part of the framework name "LEGO-RL: Harness-Native Reinforcement Learning for Coding Agents" [32]. The paper describes LEGO-RL as a framework that bridges native coding-agent harnesses with scalable policy-gradient optimization without modifying their internal control flow [32]. It is built upon three pillars: (1) faithful optimization via in-process LLM proxying to capture raw generation streams and maintain token-level alignment, (2) reliable execution via scalable sandbox orchestration with image caching and defenses against reward hacking, and (3) observable training through an integrated plugin for validation and monitoring with a Live UI for trajectory diagnostics [32]. The authors evaluate LEGO-RL by training the Qwen3.5-35B-A3B model across three native coding-agent harnesses, showing improvements in coding performance on SWE-bench Verified (from 64.0% to 70.4% on OpenHands SDK, 62.4% to 68.2% on Claude Code, and 57.2% to 66.6% on OpenCode) while maintaining a high rollout-training probability correlation above 0.99 [32].

F11.question: Vad hände i forskningen förra veckan?
F11.answer:
Based on the sources provided for the time range of 2026-09-07 to 2026-09-13, several significant research developments occurred in the AI field:

Researchers introduced Uno, a new class of models that achieves lossless speedups in LLMs by using diffusion to draw multiple tokens in parallel from an AR model distribution, delivering up to 3x speedups over base AR models [1].

The field saw the introduction of multiple new benchmarks, including SAEScientist-Bench for evaluating AI agents conducting autonomous SAE interpretability research [9], MetroLLM-Bench for testing language models as transit kiosk policies covering six real metro systems [10], and WearableQA for health reasoning over real-world wearable data with 4,084 questions [26].

Several new methods for improving language models were proposed, including RISE (Recursive Improvement via Self-Extrapolating Policy Distillation) which constructs a synthetic teacher directly from the model's own RLVR training trajectory [4], and TGOPD (Teacher-Gated On-Policy Distillation) which verifies teacher reliability at the prompt level before applying dense supervision [3].

The 2026 PNPL competition was announced, introducing LibriBrain100, an extended dataset for word classification that enables cross-subject generalization with as little as 10 minutes of subject-specific fine-tuning data [21].

Researchers also introduced DF26, a novel benchmark for detecting AI-generated videos that shows human performance and deepfake detectors are close to random chance [13], and MOLE, an open benchmark for detecting insider threats in AI agents with 150 AI-operated accounts and 12 threats [5].

Additional research included the Discovery Certification Protocol (DCP) for auditing AI research agents [6], and the Critical Review of On-Policy Self-Distillation that identifies collapse as a symptom governed by three levers [7].

F15.question: Vad har hänt med AI-agenter den senaste veckan, i både papers och videor?
F15.answer:
In the last week (2026-09-11 to 2026-09-17), several significant developments in AI agents were reported across papers and videos:

GPT-6 Astra has been highlighted as enabling "AI software factories" where agents can autonomously build applications through continuous execution [4]. These factories allow agents to run 24/7, accepting GitHub issues to build out applications without human intervention [17].

Claude Code has emerged as a popular "skill" that drives computer use by controlling screens, validating environments, and making decisions about whether computer use is necessary [9]. This skill is designed to be adaptable across operating systems while avoiding security risks like prompt injection attacks [13].

Research has advanced in agent safety with HazardAuditor, an execution-grounded framework that improves safety accuracy by up to 16.5 percentage points over prior guards [7]. This addresses the gap between static content safety and runtime behavior for computer-use agents.

RSIAgent has been developed for recursive self-improvement through autonomous memory construction, enabling agents to adapt to new environments without retraining [18]. This framework helps open-source models like Kimi-K3 outperform frontier closed-source models including GPT-6.

Atria Dawn Preview has been introduced as a foundation agentic language model for scientific research and engineering workflows, achieving competitive results across 16 benchmarks [22]. The research also documented how humans increasingly partner with agents at the project level rather than just task execution.

Emergence World has been created as a multi-agent environment for adversarial stress-testing of long-horizon autonomous systems, revealing that individually capable agents can form systems with qualitatively different failure modes [25].

Occamy-1.0 has been released as a cost-efficient co-work model obtained by further training Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, demonstrating strong performance across co-work benchmarks while remaining competitive with larger models [3].

AI agents are beginning to make purchases, with Stripe building systems that allow agents to handle transactions within defined budgets (e.g., buying coffee) while maintaining trust [28]. The research indicates trust levels are rising rapidly for specific, well-defined tasks.

Omochi (referred to as "Omarchy" in videos) has been presented as a desktop environment making agent computing possible, with agent guidance covering configuration changes, top bar management, and visibility into agent activity at the OS level [6].

AI second brains are evolving into team brains, with content showing how to extend personal AI knowledge bases to collaborative environments and improve productivity across teams [19].
